cards.claim: Smaller training image size enables larger batch sizes due to GPU/TPU memory constraints, improving training throughput
cards.conditions: EfficientNet-B6 on ImageNet ILSVRC2012; TPUv3 cores and V100 GPUs; batch sizes 12-128; training image sizes 380-512px
cards.effect: Training speed improvement up to 2.2x when reducing training size from 512px to 380px
cards.evidence: Table 2 empirical measurements: batch=128 at size=512 causes OOM, but batch=128 at size=380 achieves 93 imgs/sec/core on TPU (vs 42 at size=512 with batch=32)
cards.quote: As shown in Table 2, smaller image size leads to less computations and enables large batch size, and thus improves training speed by up to 2.2x.

cards.claim: For the same network architecture, smaller image sizes require weaker regularization (lower augmentation magnitude) for optimal accuracy, while larger image sizes benefit from stronger regularization
cards.conditions: ConvNet model sampled from EfficientNetV2 search space; ImageNet; three image sizes (128, 192, 300px); RandAug magnitudes 5-15; mean/stdev over 3 runs
cards.effect: Accuracy varies by 0.5-1.5 pp across augmentation magnitudes; small images optimal at magnitude=5 (78.3%), large images at magnitude=15 (83.2%)
cards.evidence: Table 5 showing top-1 accuracy across image sizes and augmentation magnitudes with low variance across runs
cards.quote: When image size is small, it has the best accuracy with weak augmentation; but for larger images, it performs better with stronger augmentation.

cards.claim: Progressive learning can be structured into discrete stages: early stages with small image size and weak regularization, later stages with larger image sizes and stronger regularization, all within a fixed total training budget
cards.conditions: EfficientNetV2-S/M/L on ImageNet ILSVRC2012; 350 epochs total; 4 stages (~87 epochs each); RMSProp optimizer with warmup-then-decay LR schedule
cards.effect: Enables 3-9x training speedup vs EfficientNet-B7 while improving final accuracy (85.7% vs 84.7%)
cards.evidence: Table 6 and Table 7: minimum and maximum image sizes and regularization magnitudes for S/M/L; Table 7 training times in hours on 32 TPU cores
cards.quote: For progressive learning, we divide the training process into four stages with about 87 epochs per stage: the early stage uses a small image size with weak regularization, while the later stages use larger image sizes with stronger regularization, as described in Algorithm 1.

cards.claim: Using smaller image size for training than inference (FixRes approach) maintains or slightly improves accuracy while enabling larger batch sizes and faster training, without requiring post-training finetuning
cards.conditions: EfficientNet-B6 on ImageNet ILSVRC2012; training at 380px vs inference at full resolution; batch sizes 12-128; TPUv3 and V100
cards.effect: Training throughput 76-93 imgs/sec at 380px vs 42 at 512px; accuracy 84.6% at 380px vs 84.3% at 512px (slight improvement, not drop)
cards.evidence: Table 2 showing throughput and accuracy; authors note this differs from prior FixRes work which required finetuning
cards.quote: A simple improvement is to apply FixRes (Touvron et al., 2019), by using a smaller image size for training than for inference... Notably, as pointed out in (Touvron et al., 2020; Brock et al., 2021), using smaller image size for training also leads to slightly better accuracy. But unlike (Touvron et al., 2019), we do not finetune any layers after training.

cards.claim: Progressive learning with adaptive regularization maintains the same warmup-then-decay learning rate schedule throughout all image size stages
cards.conditions: EfficientNetV2 on ImageNet ILSVRC2012; 350 epochs; RMSProp optimizer; 4 progressive stages
cards.effect: Learning rate warmed up once at start (0 to 0.256), then decayed globally (0.97× every 2.4 epochs) across all stages; no lr adjustment at stage transitions
cards.evidence: Described in setup section; Algorithm 1 shows image size and regularization change per stage but learning rate schedule unchanged
cards.quote: Learning rate is first warmed up from 0 to 0.256, and then decayed by 0.97 every 2.4 epochs.

cards.claim: Different model sizes (S/M/L) use different maximum regularization strengths during progressive training, with larger models using stronger regularization despite identical minimum values and image size schedule
cards.conditions: EfficientNetV2-S/M/L on ImageNet ILSVRC2012; same image size progression (128→300/380px) across all sizes; stage-wise linear interpolation
cards.effect: EfficientNetV2-S uses RandAug 5→15 and dropout 0.1→0.3; EfficientNetV2-L uses RandAug 5→25 and dropout 0.1→0.5; maintains accuracy across model scales
cards.evidence: Table 6 showing min/max regularization parameters for S, M, L models with explanation that 'larger models generally require more regularization to combat overfitting'
cards.quote: For simplicity, all models use the same minimum values of size and regularization, but they adopt different maximum values, as larger models generally require more regularization to combat overfitting.
